newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates steady despite major outflows.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates steady despite major outflows.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed steady at 3.75-4.00 percent on Tuesday, against the day's opening of 3.50-4.50 percent, dealers said.
There was some demand for call rates at 4.0 percent, said Suhas Sahakari, Senior Manager Treasury, UTI Bank.
"It will continue below 5.0 percent for the rest of the fortnight," he said.

The current levels of call rates shows that the repos auction, which mopped up 22.0 billion rupees and the state loan, which may have received application for 25.0 billion rupees, could not have impacted the market, dealers said.
The security prices could not see any major movements as the dealers were not ready to take positions, bankers said.
The volume on National Stock Exchange was lower at 2.30 billion rupees on Tuesday against the previous day's 3.27 billion rupees, dealers said.
The 13.40 percent 1999 stock was steady at 100.95 rupees, dealers said.
The treasury bills maturing in January 1998 were traded at 10.25 yield compared to previous yield of 10.28 percent.
There was no activity in commercial paper and certificates of deposits on Tuesday, dealers said.
